findings.title: Shutdown grace is not actually guaranteed to bound one Runner tick; shipped defaults violate the invariant
findings.description: `validate_settings` enforces `tick_call_timeout_seconds < shutdown_grace_seconds`, justified by its docstring as "so a stop waits for at most one call." But a tick's worst-case duration is `tick_deadline_seconds + tick_call_timeout_seconds`: calls may start until the deadline passes, and a call starting just inside the deadline may then run for its full `tick_call_timeout_seconds`. With the shipped defaults (`ProcessSettings`: deadline 5.0, call 8.0, grace 10.0), that is 13 s > 10 s grace — and the validation accepts it. Concretely: with a SIGTERM arriving at tick start on a healthy process, the in-flight tick can legitimately still be running at the grace expiry; the CLI (`exit_on_grace_expiry=True`, see `src/amoeba/cli/lifecycle.py:44-67`) then abandons the process with `GRACE_EXPIRED` (6) and `amoeba stop` reports a timeout, even though the tenant would have returned moments later. This contradicts `shutdown_grace_seconds`'s own docstring in `src/amoeba/process/settings.py` ("It bounds one tick, not the whole shutdown") and the "larger than `tick_deadline_seconds` so one call that starts just inside the deadline still has room to finish" intent for `tick_call_timeout_seconds`: the two fields as defaulted cannot jointly satisfy it. The check should be `tick_deadline_seconds + tick_call_timeout_seconds <= shutdown_grace_seconds` (or the defaults adjusted, e.g. call timeout 4.0); the crash-proof entry (`tests/runner/crash_entry.py`, grace 5.0, deadline 5.0 + call 4.0 = 9) has the same shape and only passes because the stub's calls return instantly. Note this is exactly the class of property (tick duration under realistic call latency) a load test would catch, which connects to the next finding.

findings.title: No load-tier test for the new Runner tenant's tick/subprocess path
findings.description: The Python rules' load-test tier requires that "any code on the simulation, network, concurrency, or environment-layer paths requires at least one load test exercising a realistic configuration," asserting "latency, throughput, or resource bounds — not just functional correctness," and that CI gate it for slices touching those paths. This slice puts a new subprocess-spawning tenant on every `amoeba start` tick in production: even with `PRODUCTION_PLANNERS` empty, production ticks issue budgeted `sq runs wait` polls for recovery-left in-flight entries (`InFlight` entries are deliberately left unresolved by `reconcile` in `src/amoeba/process/recovery.py`) and per-lifetime `cf` probes, and the tenant manages detached child handles via `LaunchTracker.reap`. `tests/load/` contains load tests for the other process paths (`test_crash_loop.py`, `test_recovery_scale.py`, `test_inbox_concurrent.py`, `test_verdict_concurrent.py`, `test_cf_watch_load.py`, `test_serve_load.py`, `test_feed_and_detection_load.py`) but none asserting bounds on the Runner's tick time, call counts, or child-lifetime hygiene under a realistic multi-project/multi-link configuration (I did not read `test_crash_loop.py` in full, so if it drives the Runner through `start` with such assertions, please treat this as verified-against that file). The crash harness in `tests/runner/` proves correctness of crash points, not resource/latency bounds, and would not have caught the grace arithmetic above.

findings.title: Stub `sq` does not model `--version`, so every start-based test logs a capture warning and records `unavailable`
findings.description: `cli_environment` now prepends the stub `sq` to PATH for all CLI tests, but the stub (`tests/sq_stub.py`) only handles `runs wait`, `run`, and `runs prune`; `sq --version` falls through to its "unexpected arguments" branch and exits 2, so `capture_sq_version_label` (called by `standard_tenants` on every `start`) logs a warning and records `VERSION_UNAVAILABLE`. This is safe by design of `capture_version_label` (no test asserts on the sq label), but it means persistent warning noise in the output of every `start`-driven test. Adding a trivial `--version` branch to the stub (as `detection_e2e_harness.py` already does with `FAKE_SQ_LABEL`) would keep those logs clean. Separately, in `tests/runner/test_end_to_end.py`, `tick_until("the shape error", lambda: False)` uses an impossible predicate and relies on `UpstreamShapeError` to break out; it fails correctly but only after the full 20 s wait if the raise ever regresses — a small clarity trap worth a dedicated helper if the pattern grows.
